headline: Leafs’ Chris Tanev week-to-week with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev is week-to-week with an upper-body injury after being placed on injured reserve earlier in the week, and that John Tavares left a game after collapsing when Sabres forward Josh Norris slid into his legs early in the third period.

The injuries land on a team whose results are running ahead of its play. TOR sits at 3-3-2 with just 44.7% of the expected goals so far this season (44% at 5-on-5), yet it is 3.6 goals above expected, with its goaltending 3.2 goals saved above expected. That cushion can vanish quickly, and losing bodies makes it harder to hold. Tanev's own numbers are modest in a six-game sample: 40.76% of 5-on-5 expected goals, and TOR's share is 2.93 points worse with him on the ice. His absence may matter more for role and minutes (16.84 per game) than for any dramatic drop in quality. For BUF, Norris has one goal and 1.24 expected goals from his own shots in eight games, so his scoring is roughly in line with his chances. The Sabres are 4-3-1 and slightly better than their record, with 51.8% of the expected goals, though their goaltending sits 5.8 goals below expected.
